value.overview: The Melodious Blackbird (Dives dives) is a medium-sized New World blackbird of the family Icteridae. Adults are almost entirely black, often with a subtle blue or violet gloss, and have a rounded, moderately broad tail. It is known for clear, varied whistles and loud territorial duets. The species occurs from Mexico through Central America and has reached Costa Rica, where it is now recorded regularly in suitable lowland and middle-elevation habitats.
value.classification: The Melodious Blackbird belongs to the order Passeriformes and the blackbird and oriole family, Icteridae. It is the only widely recognized species in the genus Dives in much of its range; the closely related Scrub Blackbird is treated separately by most modern authorities.
value.identification: This is a fairly large, stocky blackbird measuring about 23–26 cm. Adults are uniformly black, with a noticeable bluish sheen in good light; the bill, eyes, legs, and feet are dark. The tail is medium length, rounded, and broad rather than deeply forked. Females are usually duller than males, while immature birds are browner and less glossy. Its pointed bill helps distinguish it from cowbirds, and its loud, musical whistles are distinctive.
value.rangeHabitat: The Melodious Blackbird ranges from coastal eastern and southeastern Mexico south through Central America to Costa Rica. In Costa Rica it occurs as a resident, with records from several regions and increasing reports since its first documented national records in the late twentieth century. It favors open and semi-open landscapes, including pasture edges, agricultural boundaries, second-growth vegetation, scrub, scattered trees, forest edges, stream margins, gardens, and areas near human settlements. It is generally associated with lowlands and foothills but may occur at moderate elevations.
value.migrationStatus: It is considered non-migratory and resident across its range. In Costa Rica, birds are present year-round rather than arriving as regular seasonal migrants, although local movements may occur in response to food and habitat conditions.
value.breeding: Pairs defend territories with loud songs, duets, bill-up displays, and aggressive encounters with intruders. The nest is usually placed in vegetation, often in a tree or shrub, although detailed information on nesting in Costa Rica is limited. Breeding is generally associated with the rainy season or periods of favorable food availability, but timing varies geographically. Both members of a pair participate in territorial defense, and the species may nest in human-modified landscapes where suitable cover and feeding areas remain.
value.dietFeeding: The Melodious Blackbird feeds on a wide variety of foods. It commonly forages on the ground in open areas, probing or opening material with its bill, and also searches through trees and shrubs. Fruits are important when available, while other foods may include seeds, insects, and additional small invertebrates. In Costa Rica it can feed in pastures, gardens, forest edges, cultivated areas, and around buildings, often moving through open ground and low vegetation.
value.behavior: This active blackbird is conspicuous because of its strong voice and territorial behavior. Pairs may sing together in coordinated duets and use upright postures or short attacks to defend feeding and nesting areas. Individuals forage both on the ground and in the canopy, sometimes joining other birds in open habitats. The species often tolerates or benefits from moderately disturbed environments and may be seen along roadsides, pasture margins, gardens, and suburban green spaces.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population trend is not clearly quantified, but the species is not regarded as undergoing a meaningful overall decline. In Costa Rica, its distribution appears to have expanded since it was first documented there, and it is now regularly reported in suitable areas.
